signature: Single-ping interference bursts about 2 m long at random range, up to -18 dB Sv on ES70, bleeding weakly into ES200 on the same pings; 1 to 15% of ES70 samples flagged
where seen: F2 (ES70 and ES200 echograms), F3; every HB2305 file
mitigation: Two-sided ping-to-ping impulse filter (Ryan et al. 2015), echofind.io.ek80.impulse_mask. For a handheld near boats and other divers' sonars: coded or frequency-agile pulses plus the same ping-to-ping test

signature: Whole listening window raised 15 to 70 dB in 10 to 37% of ES70 pings (multi-ping, so the two-sided test misses it); another sounder firing at its own rate
where seen: F3 far range; interference_ping_frac in data/interim/w1/noaa/summary.csv (five of seven 500 m records)
mitigation: Estimate noise as the median over pings; drop pings whose passive window exceeds the median by 6 dB; never set a threshold from a ping mean

signature: Noise amplified by TVG: noise-equivalent Sv rises as 20 log r + 2 alpha r; at 200 kHz it overtakes the water-column signal beyond about 70 to 90 m
mitigation: SNR mask (Sv minus noise-equivalent Sv above 10 dB) before detection; the maximum useful range per frequency comes from this curve, which sets the handheld's 10/20/50 m modes

signature: Seabed multiples at 2x and 3x the seabed range (about 78 and 117 m here), 30 to 40 dB below the first echo
mitigation: Gate detections short of the first multiple, or flag multiple ranges as excluded; in 10 to 20 m of water the multiples fall inside a 50 m display

signature: Near-field and near-surface scattering (bubbles, ring-down) in the first 1 to 8 m, varying from ping to ping
where seen: F2 top rows, F3 left of 8 m; impulse flags 1.7% within 10 m on ES200
mitigation: Blank the near field; start statistics at 8 m; for a handheld held just below the surface this blank zone sets the minimum detection range

signature: Noise floor varies by 17 to 19 dB between files on ES18, ES38 and ES70 (22 Jul 05:39 and 23 Jul 04:51 are noisiest); ES200 varies by under 5 dB
mitigation: Per-session or per-ping noise estimate (passive listening or far range) feeding CFAR; no fixed thresholds

signature: Heavy-tailed envelope at FM resolution (cm-scale cells): K shape nu about 0.5 to 1.3 in open water, near the bottom and in the seabed echo; Rayleigh rejected in 90 of 92 windows
mitigation: Set CFAR thresholds from K or Weibull fits, or use OS-CFAR; GO-CFAR at seabed edges (H3, W2). Report false-alarm rates at the fitted tail, not the Rayleigh tail

signature: Tails heavier than even the fitted K above P = 1e-2 (fish and plankton mixed with the background): a single-component model under-predicts rare strong echoes
mitigation: Use mixture models (K plus outliers) for threshold setting; treat strong single echoes as candidates for the classifier, not as noise to be thresholded away

signature: Discrete scattering layers (fish, plankton) at 10 to 30 m, strongest at 38 kHz
mitigation: Multi-frequency response and track persistence separate biology from a stationary body; dual frequency is a feature, not only a range trade

signature: Seabed echo fluctuates 2.3 to 3.0 dB (sd) from ping to ping, well under the 5.6 dB of Rayleigh fading; seabed range changes 1.5 m over 3 minutes
mitigation: Use the seabed as an in-situ gain reference; average 3 to 5 pings for seabed-relative features; track the seabed with a running median

signature: Frequency-dependent seabed SNR: ES200 is 20 to 30 dB below ES38 (absorption and lower power)
mitigation: Pair a low frequency (range and penetration) with a high one (resolution) in the dual-frequency design

signature: Persistent narrowband tones near 86, 103 and 120 kHz, 10 to 28 dB above the local floor, present in every season
mitigation: Notch or avoid these bands; check one's own electronics for the same tones, since handheld sonars operate at 100 to 800 kHz

signature: Recorder limits: flat electronic floor near -151 dBFS^2/Hz above 10 kHz in quiet periods; anti-alias roll-off above 100 kHz
mitigation: Treat MBARI as valid only below 100 kHz; noise at handheld frequencies needs another source or the simulator's thermal-noise term

signature: Nearby vessel: 10 to 15 dB broadband rise, an 11 to 12 kHz sounder ping train, impulsive transients; envelope becomes heavy-tailed (K nu 1.8, SI 4.0)
mitigation: Adaptive noise estimate and impulse blanking; this is the realistic worst case for a rescuer working near boats

signature: Biological sounds: song-like units at 0.2 to 5 kHz and broadband transients up to 20 to 30 kHz (July 2024)
mitigation: Out of band for an active sonar above 100 kHz; relevant only as label noise for passive detectors

signature: Low-frequency fluctuation below 500 Hz of 3 to 6 dB (distant shipping, flow and cable noise)
mitigation: High-pass filter; negligible at sonar frequencies

signature: Sonar-band (60 to 120 kHz) noise is Gaussian when quiet: envelope Rayleigh in January, April and July (SI 0.95 to 1.01)
mitigation: Gaussian noise is a sound simulator default; add a vessel-transient mode for the heavy-tailed case
